title: Assessing the cardiovascular and potassium lowering effects of levalbuterol compared to albuterol: a randomized control trial
authors: Shebli B, Ghabally M, Shabouk MB, Arnaout AY, Zeina MB, Malhis M
population: Patients older than 16 years with serum potassium above 5.9 mEq/l at Aleppo University Hospital, half with chronic kidney disease
funder: The author(s) declare that no financial support was received for the research and/or publication of this article.
result: Single-centre, single-blinded trial. All patients received 10 IU insulin with 25 g glucose, adjusted for renal function, plus nebulised albuterol 10 mg or levalbuterol 5 mg. Mean baseline potassium was 6.68 mEq/l (SD 0.43) in the albuterol group and 6.59 mEq/l (SD 0.46) in the levalbuterol group. Potassium fell by 1.31 mEq/l (SD 1.19, n = 10) at 90 min with albuterol and by 0.74 mEq/l (SD 0.45, n = 15) with levalbuterol (p = 0.176). Heart rate rose by 17.27 beats/min (SD 10.66, n = 12) and 12.00 beats/min (SD 11.42, n = 18) at 30 min (p = 0.214). Tremor and nervousness were the symptoms reported most often.
